newsitem.title: UK: Europe crude outlook - gas oil fallout limited.
newsitem.headline: Europe crude outlook - gas oil fallout limited.

text.p: The European crude oil market may suffer some fallout this week from a reversal in the fortunes of market leader gas oil but the steep Brent backwardation, among other factors, will continue to work in sellers' favour.
North Sea distillate-rich crudes like Oseberg could struggle to sustain premiums at 50 cents over Brent if gas oil premiums, lose more ground from recent records, dealers said.
"The fall in gas oil and the relative strength of gasoline, means the shine is off distillate crudes here," said one senior European trader.
"In principle you should see grades like Oseberg suffer a little but not so much Ekofisk and Statfjord."
Dealers on Monday were still trying to assess the impact of gas oil's heavy correction late last week which knocked a hole in record crack spread premiums.
Gas oil cargo premiums over benchmark Dated Brent, having climbed from just $3.60 in mid-August, slipped from a post Gulf war record $10.45 on October 2 to $7.50 on Friday.
"Refining margins are still very good because fuel and gasoline have made up for some of the fall on gas oil," said a trader.

North Sea loading programmes, due out on Monday and Tuesday, are set to show a return to full capacity flows with the return from maintenance at the end of October of Norway's 440,000 barrel a day (bpd) Gullfaks field.
Traders said the extra cargoes, an additional ten Gullfaks, might weigh on markets.
On the upside, Brent's backwardation already has attracted term contract buyers to signal their preference for cargoes loading at the beginning of November, traders said.
At first glance renewed transatlantic shipments, given a Brent/WTI arbitrage below a dollar a barrel, appears limited.
But dealers said reasonable VLCC freight and fresh buying interest in the U.S. Gulf for spot North Sea crude might also work to help keep a floor under North Sea differentials.
Nigerian grades, in demand from three continents, could only prove a winner this week, traders said.
Improving differentials were masked last week by Nigerian contract holders desperate to keep a lid on the market ahead of next week's release by NNPC of November pricing.
Nigerian values were helped by Taiwanese CPC's decision not to opt out of its term contract purchases from Elf for November despite poor economics dictated by a wide Brent/Dubai spread.

CPC will take two November VLCCS, shared three parts Forcados one part Angolan Palanca aboard one and three Forcados one Odudu on the second, traders said. Six Qua Iboe already are committed to India's November purchase tender.
Dealers said light grades could easily improve on this week's Brent plus 70 cents while Forcados might sail above Brent plus 80 cents.

Urals, boosted by rising fuel oil, also was set to get a helping hand from four day's of pipeline maintenance at Novorossiisk. The Russian grade could improve 10-15 cents to reach Brent less 60-65 cents cif Med, dealers said.
